speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what you're experiencing, can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing? Does anyone observe shaking or loss of bladder control?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he have any history of head trauma or febrile seizures, and does he experience any sensory changes like flashing lights or unusual smells before the episodes? I will also request an EEG to look for seizure activity. REQUEST TEST: EEG

text: The muddy taste and post-episode confusion strongly suggest a temporal lobe origin, which aligns perfectly with the EEG findings. To further characterize the structural cause, I will request brain imaging. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, this points toward idiopathic focal epilepsy rather than a structural lesion. Do the episodes occur more frequently during sleep or upon waking, and does he have any family history of seizures?

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste is a classic gustatory aura for temporal lobe epilepsy, and the EEG confirms right-sided focus. I have enough information to make a diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
